gga-vqe-one-shot-local-selection: Section 1, p.3: the authors define GGA-VQE as selecting operator and angle in one shot with a frozen core; Section 4.3 p.15 repeats it. Design statement, not a result.
gga-vqe-not-for-strongly-correlated-with: Section 1, p.3-4: authors state they do not expect accurate strongly correlated results without post-processing; scope limit on own method.
gga-vqe-hardware-setup-ionq-aria: Section 2, p.4: states device, SDK and 2500 shots.
gga-vqe-molecular-basis-and-active-space: Section 2, p.4: STO-3G and active spaces stated as setup.

gga-vqe-iteration-cap-40: Section 2.1, p.5: the cap is setup; the 'very optimistic' reason is attributed to the authors in the value ('they consider').
gga-vqe-ising-parameters: Section 2.2, p.6: h=0.5, J=0.2 stated as setup.
gga-vqe-ising-easy-classically-limit: Section 2.2, p.8: authors state their Ising test is highly structured and not hard classically, and that it only assesses a simple problem. Limit on own experiment; type should be limit/scope.
gga-vqe-two-primary-challenges: Section 3, p.9: authors state which challenge the study addresses ('we focus on the latter'). The challenge list itself is their framing; the value attributes it.

The pool property B^3=B is shown by direct calculation only for the double-qubit generator; others are 'similar', not given. The identity itself is complete.
gga-vqe-hybrid-measurement-not-scalable: Section 4.5, p.17: authors admit the hybrid evaluation is not scalable because it needs classical emulation.
gga-vqe-hybrid-scope-r1-only: Section 4.5, p.17: authors state they focus on R1 and that R3 studies are beyond scope.
gga-vqe-qeb-circuits-not-most-efficient: Appendix 5.1, p.18: authors note the QEB circuits they used are not the most hardware-efficient. (Value says Section 5.1; text is on PDF p.18.)
gga-vqe-data-code-on-request: Data and Code availability, p.18: the paper's own availability statement.
gga-vqe-competing-interest-qubit-pharma: Competing interests p.18 gives the shareholder disclosure; affiliation 2 on p.1 shows Qubit Pharmaceuticals Advanced Research Department. 'Employs several authors' is read from the affiliations, not the quote.
ferrie-qubit-two-complex-numbers: Myth 2, PDF p.58 (printed p.50, anchor uses PDF pages): 'In short, a qubit is represented not by 0 and 1 at the same time but by two complex numbers. These numbers take on a continuum of values.' Quotes confirmed on that page. The book's own plain-language definition.
ferrie-book-license-cc-by-nc-nd: Copyright notice, PDF p.4: 'This work is licensed under CC BY-NC-ND 4.0.' Confirmed on that page.
book-omits-complexity-caveats: Myth 5, PDF p.106 (printed p.98, matching the stored anchor): the author states the book omits complexity caveats for brevity. Quote confirmed on PDF p.106; a statement about the book's own scope.
ferris-aim-tutorial-code-open: Abstract, p.1: authors state the example simulation they provide and that all source code is freely available. Confirmed on p.1.
ferris-hardware-ibm-lagos-7-qubit: Section I, p.1: all quantum simulations ran on ibm_lagos; code in an openly available Jupyter notebook using Qiskit (same paragraph).
ferris-tight-binding-model-setup: Section VI, p.5: five-site chain, defect between sites two and three, hopping tau_d not equal tau (text layer drops the 'not equal' sign), single particle, spin ignored; Eq. 29.
ferris-initial-state-and-time-range: Section VI, p.6: initial state |00001> in Qiskit little-endian notation, time range 0 to 4 pi (Figure 3 text), computed classically.
ferris-error-mitigation-definition: Section VII, p.6: the authors define error mitigation in their own words (with ref 37 as support), and describe it as a collection of methods that suppress noise.
ferris-mapomatic-layout-selection: Section VII.A, p.7: authors describe the layout tool they used and state Fig. 4c was best at execution time, with scores listed in the Figure 4 caption. Single and two-qubit gate errors and measurement errors are named on p.7.
ferris-fidelity-heuristic-eq35: Section VII.B, p.7: Eq. 35, f_circuit = f1^N1Q * f2^N2Q, is the authors' own defined heuristic. The value matches Eq. 35.
ferris-post-selection-bitstring-rule: Section VII.E, p.9: the authors state which bitstrings are accepted (one 1 and four 0s) and that others are ignored in post-processing.
ferris-results-setup-m8-10000-shots: Section VII.F, p.9: m = 8 chosen 'to illustrate the significant improvements achievable with error mitigation' and 10,000 executions to reduce shot noise.
ferris-combined-mitigation-components: Section VII.F, p.9: layout from mapomatic, full confusion matrix for SPAM, native RZX rewrite, transpiler passes and post-selection are listed as the combined optimization.
fey-rdl-contributions-listed: Section 1, p.4: the authors list their contributions (blueprint, RelBench beta with two databases and two tasks each, research program). The paper has no experiments in this version; this is scope only.
fey-relational-db-three-characteristics: Section 2.1, p.5: the three characteristics are stated as the data model the paper works with.
fey-formal-relational-db-definition: Section 2.1, p.5: formal definition of a relational database (T, L) with entity tuple v = (p, K, x, t).
fey-fact-vs-dimension-tables: Section 2.1, p.5: dimension and fact tables are described, including that fact tables usually carry a dedicated time column (text on p.5, outside the two quotes).
fey-training-labels-from-history: Section 2.2, p.6: 'Our key insight is that we can generate training labels using historical data'; labels computed from history when the window ends before the latest timestamp. A design rule of the framework, shown with an example, not a measured result.
fey-training-table-definition: Section 2.2, p.6: training table entities v = (K, t, y), no input data x.
fey-temporal-consistency-rule: Section 2.2, p.6: the rule t_u <= t_v is the paper's stated consistency condition.
fey-training-table-task-formats: Section 2.2, p.6 to p.7: node-level (ENTITYID, LABEL, TIME) and link-level (SOURCEENTITYID, TARGETENTITYID, LABEL, TIME) columns; temporal tasks need a seed time, non-temporal tasks impute missing values (p.7).
fey-training-table-sql-generation: Section 2.2, p.7: stated procedure for building training tables with time-conditioned SQL queries.
fey-schema-graph-definition: Section 3.1, p.7: schema graph (T, R), R = L union L^-1; inverse links ensure all tables are reachable.
fey-relational-entity-graph-definition: Section 3.2, p.8: definition of G = (V, E, phi, psi) with time mapping tau; -infinity for non-temporal rows.
fey-temporal-neighbor-sampling-strategie: Section 3.3, p.8 to p.9 and Algorithm 1 (p.8): three sampling strategies are defined.
fey-gnn-architecture-three-stage: Section 3.4, p.9: the three-stage generic architecture is defined as the blueprint.
fey-temporal-neighborhood-filter: Section 3.4.1, p.10: Equation 4 defines the time-filtered neighborhood; the sentence that it naturally respects time follows directly from the definition.
fey-node-and-link-model-heads: Section 3.4.2, p.10: node-level and link-level heads defined; generalization to |K|>2 stated; the same page says RelBench provides node-level tasks only.
fey-multimodal-encoders-pytorch-frame: Section 3.4.3, p.10: modality-specific encoders, pre-trained text and image encoders, tabular deep models for fusion, and PyTorch Frame in practice.
fey-relbench-modules: Section 1, p.4: the three modules are listed; PyTorch Geometric is named on p.4 for GNN models.
fey-relbench-tasks-overview: Section 1, p.4: two databases and four tasks; Stack Exchange has 7 tables, Amazon books has 3.
fey-relbench-temporal-split-rules: Section 4.2, p.12: validation and test timestamps and test-window rule are the benchmark's own protocol.
fey-relbench-default-train-table: Section 4.2, p.12: default training-table construction (timestamps from t_val - delta backwards with stride delta, entity filter, label per pair).
fey-rel-amazon-statistics: Section 4.3, p.12: statistics and timestamps of the authors' own dataset.
fey-rel-amazon-ltv-task: Section 4.3.1, p.12 to p.13: task definition, active-user filter (reviewed in the past two years), MAE metric and target range stated for the authors' own task.
fey-rel-amazon-churn-task: Section 4.3.2, p.13: task definition, active-user filter, AP metric.
fey-rel-stackex-statistics: Section 4.4, p.13 to p.14: dump date on p.13, statistics and timestamps on p.14, for the authors' own dataset.
fey-rel-stackex-engage-task: Section 4.4.1, p.14: task definition, active-user filter (at least one comment, post or vote), AP metric.
fey-rel-stackex-votes-task: Section 4.4.2, p.14: task definition, question filter (past 2 years), MAE metric, target range 0 to 52.
fey-localized-learning-open-question: Section 5.1, p.15: authors call scaling deep local models with no prior knowledge an open question for their approach.
fey-full-resolution-graph-property: Section 5.2, p.15: the authors define the property they treat as essential (full-resolution, exact encoding).
fey-stale-links-drift-open: Section 5.2, p.16: the authors state stale links may hurt and gradual drift is an open question. Hedged and untested, but stated as their own open problem.
fey-frozen-feature-extractors-suboptimal: Section 5.4, p.17: the authors state their pre-extracted frozen features are likely suboptimal. A stated limit of their own pipeline; untested.
fey-conclusion-roadmap-not-results: Section 7, p.18: authors call the paper a road map that introduces a blueprint and RelBench; consistent with no experiments in this version.
fey-authors-affiliations-kumo-ai: Title block, p.1: affiliations and the RelBench website are printed there.
fey-rdl-blueprint: Abstract, p.1: 'The core idea is to view relational databases as a temporal, heterogeneous graph ...'; formally defined in Section 3.2 p.8.
fey-relbench-scope: PDF p.4 (two databases, two tasks each) and PDF p.10 ('In the first version, RELBENCH provides node-level tasks only'). The stored anchors 'pp. 3 and 8' differ from the PDF pages where the quotes sit (p.4 and p.10); the quotes are verbatim.
finet-atomtreesearch-definition: Abstract, p.1: the authors define AtomTreeSearch and its expansion step (also Section 2).
finet-actions-independent-sets-definitio: Section 2.3, p.5: collective action and independence are the paper's own definitions. The quotes are column fragments; read in context the definition holds.
finet-quantum-call-once-per-node: Section 2.3, p.5: the quantum call happens only on the first invocation for a node's state; later calls read the saved set.
finet-rydberg-blockade-encoding: Section 2.4, p.7: the blockade mechanism is how the authors encode the independence constraint on the device.
finet-annealing-not-adiabatic-heuristic: Section 2.4, p.8: pulse duration is limited, so the adiabatic condition is generally not met and annealing is used as a heuristic. Two-column text; quotes read in context.
finet-pulse-shape-fig3: Figure 3 and Section 2.4, p.8 to p.10: the authors' stated pulse schedule.
finet-proof-of-concept-5-microseconds: Section 3.2, p.9: 5 microsecond maximum evolution; evolution emulated with QuTiP, EMU-SV and EMU-MPS. The quantum step is emulated, not run on hardware.
finet-2opt-action-independence: Section 3.2, p.9: the 2-Opt action and independence are the paper's own definitions for the TSP.
finet-qubit-limit-vs-conflict-graph: Section 3.2, p.10: quantum computers only have M qubits while the conflict graph has O(N^2) vertices; three partition methods are listed in the same paragraph.
finet-simulation-phase-sa-parameters: Section 3.2, p.11: SA temperature 100, cooling 0.98, and Cp = 0.02 chosen empirically.
finet-benchmark-setup-30-instances-100-i: Section 4, p.12: 30 instances, 100 iterations, 5 samples per MWIS sampler.
finet-datasets-tsplib-and-random: Section 3.3, p.11: TSPLIB instances with 100 cities or less plus a random Euclidean generator.
finet-baseline-sa-and-ortools-settings: Section 3.4, p.12: baseline settings and Concorde optimal solutions as stated.
finet-qpu-shots-max-500: Section 4, p.13: with random partitioning there is one subgraph and five shots per node's first expansion, so 100 iterations give at most 500; the paper states the bound and the reason. Counted from its own protocol, not a measured result.
finet-tree-structure-not-sufficient: Section 4, p.15: authors state the tree-structure variations in Figure 6 do not alone explain the optimality-gap differences.
finet-improvements-simple-protocol: Section 5, p.18: authors call their annealing protocol relatively simple and their embedding straightforward; the tighter-bounds suggestion is on the same page. Improvements are suggestions, untested.
finet-funding-pasqal-canada: Acknowledgment, p.18: NSERC and Pasqal Canada Alliance grant.
finet-software-versions: Appendix A, p.18: software versions table (Python 3.11.4, QuTiP 5.1.1, EMU-SV 2.3.0, Pulser 1.6.1, OR-Tools 9.6.2534, Concorde 03.12.19).
finet-emulation-limit: Section 3.2 p.9 ('emulated using classical simulation tools') and Section 5 p.17 ('limited computational resources due to our inability to emulate our quantum protocol at a larger scale'). theory_low.gga-vqe-hardware-efficient-pool-not-part: textbook, stated not proved (F129): Section 4.2 p.12 asserts the property of a pool from ref 17 with no argument.
theory_low.gga-vqe-minimal-pool-size-2n-minus-2: Section 4.2 p.12-13: the completeness property is 'possible to show', taken from ref 17, not proved here. The 2N-2 size and 'minimal CNOT' are stated, not argued.
theory_low.gga-vqe-measurement-count-4m-plus-1: Section 4.3 p.15: count is argued in prose from the linear system (four unknowns for QEB, two for hardware-efficient). No theorem or proof; informal cost count.
theory_low.gga-vqe-energy-sorting-bottleneck-om: Section 4.3 p.16: 'main bottle-neck ... O(M)' is an asserted statement with no derivation beyond the earlier count; a claim.
theory_low.gga-vqe-ising-five-circuits-per-iteratio: Section 4.4 p.17: five-circuit grouping is argued in bullets; Equation (19) rests on 'direct calculation' in Appendix 5.3. Not a stated theorem; informal measurement-grouping argument.
theory_low.gga-vqe-general-ising-ten-circuits: Appendix 5.4 p.21: 'at most ten' follows from 'an additional five circuits' by prose argument over Tables 1-2; no proof.
theory_low.gga-vqe-two-dim-landscape-measurements: Appendix 5.5 p.22-23: 7 and 6M^2+1 counts follow from Equation (28) by prose; no proof, and 7 per pair versus 6M^2+1 is not reconciled in text.
theory_low.gga-vqe-d-tuple-measurement-scaling: Appendix 5.5 p.23: O(5^d M^d) and O(3^d M^d) come from 'similar arguments' with no derivation. The intractability remark is a stated limit, but the value joins it to the unproved scaling; graded by the weaker.

theory_low.ferrie-plus-state-equal-probability: textbook, stated not proved (F129): PDF p.69 states the property and the QRNG remark with no evidence or derivation. Quotes confirmed on PDF p.69.
